chunks: Muhammad b. Ali Majiluwayh (may God have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Bakr b. Salih. He said: Abdullah b. Ibrahim al-Ghifari narrated to us from Abd al-Rahman from his uncle Abd al-Aziz b. Ali from Sa'id b. al-Musayyib from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: Shall I not guide you to something by which God expiates sins and increases good deeds? It was said: Of course, O Messenger of God. He said: Performing ablution thoroughly despite hardships, taking frequent steps to these mosques, and waiting for prayer after prayer. There is not one among you who leaves his house purified, prays in congregation with the Muslims, then sits waiting for the next prayer, except that the angels say: O God, forgive him. O God, have mercy on him.

When you stand for prayer, straighten your rows and establish them, and close the gaps. When your imam says: God is the Greatest, then say: God is the Greatest. When he bows, then bow. When he says: God hears those who praise Him, then say: O God, our Lord, for You is all praise. Indeed, the best of rows is the first row of men, and the worst of them is the last.

key_terms.الجماعة: Congregational prayer with the Muslim community
key_terms.الخطى: Steps, referring to walking to the mosque
key_terms.الفرج: Gaps between worshippers in the prayer rows
key_terms.المكاره: Hardships, particularly discomfort such as cold or illness

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the reward for thorough ablution, walking to mosques, and waiting between prayers?
ai.summary: This hadith is narrated through Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, a prominent companion of the Prophet. The Prophet teaches three acts that expiate sins and increase good deeds: thorough ablution despite difficulty (such as cold weather), walking frequently to mosques, and waiting in the mosque between prayers. He adds that angels pray for forgiveness for those who wait between congregational prayers. The hadith then transitions to prayer etiquette, instructing the congregation to straighten rows, close gaps, follow the imam's actions, and noting that the front row is best while the rear is worst.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali Majiluwayh (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to us from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Khalid from his father from Bakr b. Salih. He said: `Abdullah b. Ibrahim al-Ghifari narrated to us from `Abd al-Rahman from his uncle `Abd al-`Aziz b. `Ali from Sa`id b. al-Musayyib from Abi Sa`id al-Khudri. He said:

The Messenger of Allah (s) said: Shall I not lead you to a thing by which Allah expiates one’s sins and increases his good deeds? It was said: Of course, O Messenger of Allah. He said: Making ablution after impurity, taking frequent steps to this Mosque, and waiting for prayer after prayer. There is not one of you who leaves his house purified, prays a prayer in congregation with the Muslims, then sits and waits for the next prayer, except that the angels say: “O Allah! Forgive him. O Allah! Have mercy on him.”

When you stand in prayer, then straighten your lines and establish them, and cover your private parts. When your imam says: “Allah is the Greatest (Allahu akbar)”, then say: “Allah is the Greatest.” When he bows, then bow. When he says: “Allah hears those who praise Him (sami`Allahu liman hamidah)”, then say: “O Allah! Our Lord, for You is all praise (Allahumma rabbana lakal hamd).” The best of lines is the first line of men, while the worst of lines is the last.
